asks: lynch_category field (Slow Grower / Stalwart / Fast Grower / Cyclical / Turnaround / Asset Play) — highest-leverage ask; half the verdicts rest on a PROVISIONAL category inferred from margin/yield/leverage shape.
Explicit long-term earnings growth rate alongside PEG — 12 of 20 names carry a negative trailing or forward PEG (earnings-decline signal, not a bargain) and the raw rate is needed to gauge severity.
Cash and net-cash-per-share to compute C10 net cash floor and C11 effective P/E — dark for AAPL, EQT and others judged on headline P/E Lynch would overrule.
Inventory and revenue for two consecutive quarters — Fail Gate 2 currently NOT_TESTABLE for all 20 names; decisive for CNH, DE, ADM, CTVA.
Long-term debt split by KIND (bank vs funded, maturity ladder) — Fail Gate 1 untestable; most important for GEN (Z 1.45), T (0.97), OKE (1.70), CNH (D/E 3.39), LNG (D/E 4.29).
Institutional ownership percentage — Fail Gate 3 half-testable on BOX and KVYO.
Payout ratio / dividend coverage — untestable on T (4.27%), OKE (4.43%), KHC (6.18% against a TTM loss), PBR (7.80%).
Sector-relative and own-history P/E context — the Stalwart test could not be run on AAPL, DE, CVX.
USD-normalized market_cap/revenue for DB (EUR) and UMC (TWD) — currently uncomparable to USD peers.
Captive-finance-arm segmentation for DE (D/E 2.29) and CNH (D/E 3.39) — consolidated D/E conflates manufacturing and finance-receivable leverage.
REIT FFO/AFFO for WELL — pe 124.59/peg 15.93 are GAAP-EPS artefacts of depreciation; verdict would be better evidenced with the operative metric.
Process ask: the fundamentals pack should precede every CHALLENGE round; add a one-line per-ticker business description so the Two-Minute Drill becomes partially answerable.
